newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates steady on buying by mills.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates steady on buying by mills.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates remained unchanged on Thursday on buying by mills and dealers said the prices would hover at these levels as the arrival of fresh supplies from the (1997/98 July-June) crop remained slow.
"Both new and old crop cotton is available for sale," dealer Shamimul Haq said. "But the moisture level is high in new arrivals as it's not fully mature yet."
He said prices would remain at the present levels because of a strong demand from mill owners.
About 150,000 bales of unsold cotton are available from the 1996/97 crop, 50,000 bales being of fine quality, dealers said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted for 2,200/2,300 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
